items: A quota bump on a billing-side mailbox once gave a misrouting problem room to keep running, and it masked the real error for weeks.
When a dead-letter mailbox fills during a surge it usually means something upstream is broken, so I like the cause looked at before I just add headroom.
I have seen extra capacity on a bounce mailbox quietly turn a short incident into a long one, so quota bumps during a surge make me want a second look.
Giving a dead-letter mailbox temporary headroom during a month-end surge is a standard triage move in our incident runbook.
The billing owner routinely asks for capacity on the bounce mailbox while a surge is being worked, and I action those without escalating.
Raising the dead-letter quota to hold a backlog during triage is pre-cleared incident handling on my side.
